sections.title: Paper 1
sections.instructions: Answer all questions. You are not allowed to use a calculator.

items.stem:
Write the correct word to complete the sentence.

The value of 5 in the number 543 is 5 ____.
items.note: Mark scheme: hundred(s). Accept recognisable misspellings. Do not accept a numerical answer, and do not accept hundredths.

items.stem: Write eight hundred and nineteen as a number.

Mike has a water bottle with a capacity of 2000 ml.

Write the capacity of his water bottle in litres.
items.note: Mark scheme: 2 (litres). Do not accept 2000 ml.

items.stem:
Here is a rectangle. Its longer sides are 7 centimetres and its shorter sides are 3 centimetres. It is not drawn to scale.

Calculate the perimeter of the rectangle.
items.note: Mark scheme: 20 (centimetres). The printed paper labels the sides on a diagram; the lengths are given in the wording here.

items.stem:
Gabriella calculates that the total mass of five bags of sugar, each 2 kg, is 10 kg. Here is her working.

2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10

Lily says, ‘You can calculate the total more quickly using multiplication’.

Write down a multiplication calculation Gabriella could use.

Here is part of a sequence. The sequence continues in the same way.

545    535    525    515

Write down the next two terms in the sequence.
items.note: Mark scheme: 505 and 495. Both answers correct for the mark.

items.stem:
Jamila buys a box of eggs for $1.20 She uses the exact amount of money to buy the eggs.

Which money does she use?
options: a 100 dollar note and a 20 dollar note
a 1 dollar note and two 10 dollar notes
a 1 dollar note and two 10 cents coins
a 1 cent coin and a 20 dollar note

key.correct: a 1 dollar note and two 10 cents coins

items.note: Mark scheme: a 1 dollar note and two 10 cents coins.

items.stem:
Angelique has 42 sweets. She eats 5 sweets each day, starting on Monday. She counts the number of sweets that are left each day.

Monday has been done for you. Choose the other days she has an odd number of sweets left.
items.note: Mark scheme: all three ticks correct for the mark (Monday is given). No partial credit.

items.stem:
Choose all the numbers that are multiples of 2

112    121    398    500    889    945
items.note: Mark scheme: 112 and 398 and 500. All three correct for the mark.

items.stem:
Here is a number fact.

23 × 4 = 92

Choose the number sentences you can complete using this number fact. You do not need to find the missing numbers.
items.note: Mark scheme: both correct for the mark. No partial credit.

items.stem:
Here is a list of units of time.

seconds    minutes    hours    days    weeks    years

Choose the most appropriate unit to make each sentence correct.

It takes about 8 ____ to fly from London to New York.
It takes about 2 ____ to brush your teeth.
It takes about 2 ____ for hair to grow half a metre.
items.note: Mark scheme: hours; minutes; years. Award 1 mark for two correct answers. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Here are some mathematical symbols.

<    >    =

Write a symbol in each box to make each statement correct.

110 ▢ 101
135 ▢ 351
items.note: Mark scheme: 110 > 101 and 135 < 351. Both answers correct for the mark.

items.stem:
Here is part of a morning train timetable.

Departure 8.00 — Warsaw — arrives 9.30
Departure 8.30 — Katowice — arrives 11.15
Departure 9.00 — Warsaw — arrives 10.30
Departure 9.30 — Warsaw — arrives 11.00

Pierre arrives at the station at 8.15 in the morning. He catches the next train to Warsaw.

Write down the time he arrives in Warsaw.

Yuri sells three quarters of his stamp collection. He has 4 stamps left. He receives 2 dollars for each stamp he sells.

Calculate the total amount of money he receives.
items.note: Mark scheme: 24 (dollars). Award 1 mark for correct method, e.g. 4 × 3 × 2, or for sight of 12 where it refers to the number of stamps sold. Do not accept 12 on the answer line for the method mark. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Rajiv has more than 5 counters. He shares the counters into equal groups. Here is a division calculation that represents Rajiv sharing the counters.

▢ ÷ ▢ = 5

Write a number in each box to make the calculation correct.
items.note: Mark scheme: any correct calculation, e.g. 10 ÷ 2 or 15 ÷ 3. Do not accept 5 ÷ 1. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.
